records.question: 32 years old female with Grave diseases with eye signs and enlarged thyroid is planned for total thyroidectomy. What can be given in the preoperative period to reduce intraoperative bleeding in the patient
records.explanation: Short-course inorganic iodide reduces thyroid hormone release and gland vascularity before selected Graves thyroidectomies. It is part of supervised preoperative preparation, generally after thionamide therapy.

records.question: First deformity corrected in CTEV?
records.explanation: In Ponseti correction of clubfoot, cavus is corrected first by aligning the forefoot with the hindfoot. Adduction and varus are then corrected together; equinus is addressed last.

records.question: Terrible triad includes injury to?
options: ACL, Medial collateral ligament and Medial Meniscus
records.explanation: The classic unhappy triad comprises the anterior cruciate ligament, medial collateral ligament and medial meniscus. Actual acute injury patterns vary, but this is the conventional named combination in the recall.

records.question: Is the following feature not a feature of optic disc in Glaucoma?
records.explanation: A Roenne nasal step is a visual-field defect. Increased cupping, vessel bayoneting and altered vessel position are optic-disc findings, so the field defect is the exception.

records.question: Which of the following is not a part of keratoconus?
records.explanation: Haab striae are horizontal breaks in Descemet membrane associated with congenital glaucoma. Keratoconus instead produces irregular astigmatism, a scissoring retinoscopy reflex and, in advanced disease, Munson sign.

records.question: Which of the following is not a feature of pterygium?
records.explanation: Pterygium shows elastotic stromal degeneration and has a head, neck and body. Simple bare-sclera excision has a substantial recurrence risk; a claimed 95% reduction in recurrence is not a feature.

records.question: Which of the following is not a feature of a complicated Cataract?
records.explanation: A Krukenberg spindle is pigment deposited on the corneal endothelium, classically in pigment dispersion. It is not a lens opacity; complicated cataract may follow uveitis and show polychromatic lustre.

records.question: Angle subtended by each optotype for 6/6 vision on a snellen chart at 6m?
records.explanation: A standard Snellen optotype subtends five minutes of arc at its designated testing distance. Each critical stroke or gap subtends one minute of arc.

records.question: All are long term reversible methods of contraception except
options: Levonorgestrel and copper containing intrauterine devices
records.explanation: Female sterilisation is intended as permanent contraception. Injections, implants and intrauterine devices are reversible, although injections are not usually grouped with user-independent LARC methods in modern classifications.

records.question: A woman with eclampsia is started on magnesium sulphate, what is the first sign of MgSO4 toxicity?
records.explanation: Loss of deep-tendon reflexes is an early clinical warning of magnesium toxicity, preceding respiratory depression at higher concentrations. Monitoring also includes breathing and urine output.

records.question: Not a component of biophysical profile:
records.explanation: The standard biophysical profile combines a nonstress test with ultrasound assessment of fetal breathing, movement, tone and amniotic fluid. Daily fetal movement counting is useful surveillance but is not one of its five scored components.

records.question: The non contraceptive uses of oral contraceptives include all except
options: Reduces the risk of ovarian Ca
Reduces the risk of endometrial Ca
records.explanation: Oral contraceptives do not protect against sexually transmitted infections, including HIV. They reduce the risk of ovarian and endometrial cancer; preventing pregnancy also reduces the absolute risk of ectopic pregnancy.

records.question: Placenta previa will show
records.explanation: Placenta praevia classically causes recurrent, painless vaginal warning bleeds. Painful bleeding with uterine tenderness suggests placental abruption instead.

records.question: Which of the following is most specific antibody for SLE
records.explanation: Anti-Smith antibodies are highly specific for systemic lupus erythematosus, although their sensitivity is limited. ANA is a sensitive screening marker; anti-dsDNA also has high specificity and can track selected disease manifestations.

records.question: Hereditary angioneurotic edema is due to deficiency of which of the following?
records.explanation: Classic hereditary angioedema types I and II involve deficient or dysfunctional C1 esterase inhibitor. Excess bradykinin causes recurrent non-urticarial swelling. Other hereditary angioedema forms can have normal C1 inhibitor.

records.question: Which of the following cytokines is not involved in our Th1 response ?
records.explanation: IL-4 favours Th2 differentiation rather than the Th1 response. IL-12 promotes Th1 development, and IFN-gamma is a characteristic Th1 effector cytokine.

records.question: Incorrect regarding Parvovirus B19 disease association with respective patients-
records.explanation: Parvovirus B19 causes erythema infectiosum, transient aplastic crises in haemolytic disorders, fetal hydrops and adult arthropathy. Polymyalgia rheumatica is not its characteristic young-adult rheumatic presentation.

records.question: Vesicular rash is seen in -
records.explanation: Hand, foot and mouth disease commonly produces vesicles on the hands and feet with oral lesions. The other listed infections more typically cause non-vesicular exanthems.

records.question: Spanish windlass is a type of strangulation mentioned below ?
records.explanation: A garrotte can use a ligature tightened with a twisting stick or similar mechanism, traditionally called the Spanish windlass. Throttling is manual neck compression; mugging uses an arm around the neck.

records.question: Cry of the fetus was heard by doctor before delivery, this is:
records.explanation: Vagitus uterinus refers to crying before complete delivery while the fetus is still within the uterus. Vagitus vaginalis describes crying while the head is still within the vagina.

records.question: Jarisch Herxheimer reaction is due to 1. IFN-Alpha 2. IL-6 3. TNF-Alpha 4. IL-8
records.explanation: The Jarisch-Herxheimer reaction is an acute inflammatory response after treatment of some spirochaetal infections. Proinflammatory mediators include TNF-alpha, IL-6 and IL-8; it is distinct from an immediate drug allergy.

records.question: Markedly reduced HDL with an ABCA1 mutation suggests which disease?
records.explanation: Tangier disease results from biallelic ABCA1 dysfunction and impaired cellular cholesterol efflux to apolipoprotein A-I. Plasma HDL cholesterol is markedly reduced.

records.question: Consider the following enzymes. 1. Glutathione peroxidase 2. Glutathione synthetase 3. Deiodinase 4. Thioredoxin reductase Which of the following enzymes used Selenocysteine?
records.explanation: Glutathione peroxidases, iodothyronine deiodinases and thioredoxin reductases include selenocysteine-containing enzymes. Glutathione synthetase is not one of these selenoenzymes.

records.question: Zellweger is a defect in biogenesis of
records.explanation: Zellweger spectrum disorders are peroxisome-biogenesis disorders, usually caused by pathogenic variants in PEX genes. Multiple peroxisomal metabolic pathways are affected.

records.question: Long term glycemic control in patients with hemolysis, is assessed by fructosamine. Fructosamine is a glycated product of
records.explanation: Fructosamine measures glycated circulating proteins, predominantly albumin, and reflects roughly the preceding two to three weeks. Altered red-cell survival can make HbA1c misleading, while albumin turnover can affect fructosamine.

records.question: Which of the following characteristics is true about stress?
options: An emotional, cognitive, physiological and autonomic response
records.explanation: Stress describes emotional, cognitive, physiological and autonomic responses to demands or threats. The other options describe more specific anxiety or illness-preoccupation experiences.

records.question: A patient of alcohol dependence with the deranged LFTs, comes in a withdrawal state. What should be given in his treatment?
records.explanation: Oxazepam undergoes glucuronidation and has no long-lived active metabolites, making it a common benzodiazepine choice when alcohol withdrawal coexists with significant liver dysfunction. Withdrawal severity and monitoring still guide treatment.

records.question: A patient is brought with altered sensorium and seizures. Attender shows the laboratory report which reveals elevated transaminases. Which of the following can be used in this condition?
records.explanation: Lorazepam is an intravenous benzodiazepine used for acute seizures. Its glucuronidation and lack of active oxidative metabolites are useful in liver dysfunction; airway monitoring remains essential.

records.question: Which of the following statements are true: A. Bedaquiline inhibits mycobacterial ATP synthase B. Pyrazinamide in enzyme inducer C. Rifampicin is used only in TB D. Isoniazid inhibits mycolic acid synthesis
records.explanation: Bedaquiline inhibits mycobacterial ATP synthase, and isoniazid inhibits mycolic-acid synthesis. Rifampicin has indications beyond tuberculosis, and pyrazinamide is not the classic hepatic enzyme inducer in this regimen.

records.question: Meropenem is indicated in treatment of A. Intra Abdominal infections B. MRSA C. Febrile neutropenia D. Diabetic foot
records.explanation: Meropenem covers many organisms causing complicated intra-abdominal infection, febrile neutropenia and selected diabetic-foot infections. It does not provide reliable MRSA coverage; these diagnoses do not mean every patient requires a carbapenem.

records.question: Metastatic calcification can be seen in all these conditions except:
records.explanation: Metastatic calcification reflects abnormal calcium-phosphate metabolism and may occur in renal failure, hyperparathyroidism or vitamin D excess. Calcium deposited in damaged metastatic nodes is ordinarily dystrophic calcification.

records.question: Iron in the tissues is stained by
records.explanation: Perls Prussian blue reaction demonstrates ferric iron in haemosiderin. Masson trichrome highlights collagen, PAS detects carbohydrate-rich substances, and Fite stain is used for mycobacteria.

records.question: Alternate procedure for height measurement in a 5 year old child?
records.explanation: Arm span can provide an alternative estimate of stature when standing height cannot be measured reliably. The relationship varies with age and body proportions, so it is an estimate rather than an exact replacement.

records.question: Find out the active metabolite of cyclophosphamide
records.explanation: Cyclophosphamide is activated by hepatic oxidation to 4-hydroxycyclophosphamide, which equilibrates with aldophosphamide. Subsequent breakdown produces the cytotoxic phosphoramide mustard and acrolein.

records.question: Which of the following ATT acts by inhibiting mycolic acid synthesis with the need of catalase enzyme?
records.explanation: Isoniazid is a prodrug activated by the mycobacterial KatG catalase-peroxidase. Its active products inhibit mycolic-acid synthesis; changes in KatG can confer resistance.

records.question: Best alternative to mother’s breast milk in a LBW/preterm child?
records.explanation: When a preterm or low-birthweight infant cannot receive sufficient mother's own milk, screened donor human milk is generally preferred where available. Fortification and nutritional monitoring depend on the infant's needs.

records.question: Which of the following diseases is X linked dominant?
records.explanation: Classic Rett syndrome is commonly associated with pathogenic MECP2 variants and an X-linked dominant pattern. Most cases arise de novo. OTC deficiency and Duchenne muscular dystrophy are X-linked recessive conditions.

records.question: Congenital absence of seminal vesicles and vas deferens is seen in
records.explanation: CFTR-related disease can cause congenital bilateral absence of the vas deferens, often with absent or hypoplastic seminal vesicles. This can occur with classic cystic fibrosis or a more limited CFTR-related phenotype.

records.question: Which of the following is more commonly associated with Kallmans syndrome?
records.explanation: Kallmann syndrome combines congenital hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with impaired smell, ranging from hyposmia to anosmia. It reflects abnormal development or migration of GnRH neurons and associated olfactory pathways.

records.question: Which one of the following constitutes the Modified Biophysical Profile?
records.explanation: The modified biophysical profile combines a nonstress test with assessment of amniotic fluid volume, traditionally the amniotic fluid index. The full profile additionally scores fetal breathing, movement and tone.

records.question: All are used as first line treatment in rheumatoid arthritis except
records.explanation: Methotrexate, sulfasalazine and hydroxychloroquine are conventional DMARDs used in initial rheumatoid arthritis treatment according to disease activity and patient factors. Azathioprine is not a usual first-line RA DMARD.

records.question: All are the features of Complicated malaria except
records.explanation: Severe malaria can involve coma, hypoglycaemia, acute kidney injury and metabolic acidosis. A pH above 7.25 is not the acidosis criterion; severe acidosis is associated with lower pH or equivalent biochemical evidence.

records.question: Technique to study DNA protein interactions?
records.explanation: DNA footprinting identifies a DNA region protected from cleavage by a bound protein. DNA fingerprinting distinguishes DNA profiles, while Northern blotting detects RNA.

records.question: Which is formed by three bones?
records.explanation: The foramen lacerum lies at the junction of sphenoid, petrous temporal and basilar occipital bones. It is largely filled by cartilage in life; the internal carotid artery passes across its superior aspect.

records.question: Which of following structure passes via jugular foramen has separate canal :
records.explanation: The glossopharyngeal nerve occupies a separate anterior compartment of the jugular foramen, divided from the vagus and accessory nerves by a fibrous septum. The hypoglossal nerve exits through the hypoglossal canal.

records.question: Stridor in a newborn is commonly seen in which of the following conditions? 1. Laryngomalacia 2. Subglottic stenosis 3. Laryngeal papilloma 4. Hemorrhagic polyp
records.explanation: Laryngomalacia and congenital subglottic stenosis can present with neonatal stridor. Laryngeal papillomatosis generally presents later, while a haemorrhagic vocal-cord polyp is not a usual neonatal cause.

records.question: Which of the following is the WRONG statement about snakebite?
options: Viperidae is vasculotoxic & anti-snake venom has to be given in systemic envenomation
records.explanation: In the usual Indian snakebite classification, cobra and krait envenoming is chiefly associated with neurotoxicity, not predominantly myotoxicity. Some elapids, especially sea snakes, are important myotoxic exceptions; venom effects can overlap.

records.question: The triad of bruise, abrasion and punctured laceration is seen in:
records.explanation: A typical firearm entrance wound combines a penetrating or punctured laceration with an abrasion collar and surrounding contusion. Appearance varies with weapon, range and intervening material; the triad is a classic description rather than a universal rule.

records.question: Under the amended Indian MTP Act, which listed gestational interval ordinarily requires opinions from at least two registered medical practitioners for eligible categories?
records.explanation: Section 3(2)(b) covers pregnancies exceeding 20 weeks but not exceeding 24 weeks in prescribed eligible categories, with opinions from at least two registered medical practitioners. Separate provisions address emergencies and specified fetal abnormalities; the interval alone does not establish eligibility.

records.question: Alongside clinical assessment, procalcitonin can help guide which decision in ventilator-associated pneumonia?
records.explanation: Procalcitonin trends may support a decision to discontinue antibiotics together with clinical assessment. They should not independently confirm VAP or select the empirical agent. The benefit is less clear when an appropriately short course is already routine.

records.question: Erythropoietin is used for which listed anaemias? 1. Nutritional anaemia; 2. CKD-related anaemia; 3. MDS-related anaemia; 4. Aplastic anaemia.
records.explanation: Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents are used in selected patients with CKD-related anaemia and selected lower-risk myelodysplastic syndromes. Iron status, endogenous erythropoietin, symptoms and risks guide selection; an ESA is not the primary treatment for a simple nutritional deficiency or aplastic anaemia.

records.question: Which of the following stains is not used to identify organisms in a post renal transplantation patient?
records.explanation: Congo red is routinely used to demonstrate amyloid rather than to identify an infecting organism. GMS and PAS help demonstrate fungi, and Fontana-Masson can highlight melanin in organisms such as Cryptococcus.

records.question: A laborer falls on an outstretched hand and has anatomical snuffbox tenderness. What is the most appropriate next step?
options: Thumb-spica cast and follow-up after 10–14 days
records.explanation: MRI can be considered for early definitive imaging of a clinically suspected scaphoid fracture after thorough examination. Immobilisation is appropriate while assessment is arranged; a normal early radiograph does not reliably exclude an occult fracture.

records.question: Which action is shared by imipramine and diphenhydramine?
records.explanation: Both drugs have antimuscarinic activity and can cause dry mouth, blurred vision, constipation and urinary retention. Imipramine is a tricyclic antidepressant; diphenhydramine is a first-generation H1 antihistamine.

records.question: Which listed drug exposure classically causes bland cholestasis?
records.explanation: Estrogens and anabolic androgenic steroids can produce bland canalicular cholestasis with little inflammatory change. Amoxicillin-clavulanate can also cause cholestatic injury, but its usual pattern is not the classic bland steroid-associated lesion.

records.question: Which of the following is incorrect?
options: Cannabis is associated with minimal withdrawal physical symptoms
Buprenorphine can be used for the management of opioid withdrawal
I.V Flumazenil is used in alcohol withdrawal long-term
records.explanation: Flumazenil antagonises benzodiazepine effects and can precipitate seizures or acute withdrawal in susceptible patients. It is not long-term alcohol-withdrawal treatment. Opioid withdrawal is usually not fatal in otherwise healthy adults, although complications can occur in vulnerable patients.

records.question: Which listed finding does not itself contraindicate breast-conserving therapy?
records.explanation: Disease confined to one quadrant does not itself rule out breast conservation when clear margins and appropriate radiotherapy are feasible. Persistently positive margins and major radiotherapy constraints require further treatment planning.

records.question: All the following are true regarding tension pneumothorax except:
options: A common cause of tension pneumothorax is positive pressure ventilation (PPV)
Thoracic spine injury can cause pneumothorax
Breath sounds are absent on the affected side
Simple pneumothorax cannot convert into a tension pneumothorax
records.explanation: A simple pneumothorax can progress to tension physiology when air enters the pleural space but cannot escape. Positive-pressure ventilation can accelerate this process, impairing ventilation and venous return.

records.question: A 60-year-old with previous MI and type 2 diabetes has LDL 130, HDL 40 and triglycerides 270 mg/dL. Which listed regimen provides appropriate secondary-prevention lipid therapy?
records.explanation: Established coronary disease calls for a high-intensity statin when tolerated. Atorvastatin 80 mg is the high-intensity choice here; the other listed statin doses are moderate intensity. Subsequent LDL response and tolerance guide any additional lipid-lowering treatment.

records.question: Hyperkalaemia and worsening renal function develop during antihypertensive treatment. Which listed drug should be withheld for assessment?
records.explanation: Losartan blocks angiotensin II signalling and lowers aldosterone, which can raise potassium. Clinically significant hyperkalaemia or renal deterioration warrants prompt assessment and may require withholding therapy. Chronic kidney disease alone is not an automatic reason to stop an otherwise indicated ARB.

records.question: Which listed exposure is least likely to cause hypocalcaemic tetany?
records.explanation: Vitamin D excess usually raises serum calcium, rather than producing the hypocalcaemia associated with tetany. Acute pancreatitis can lower calcium, and magnesium depletion can impair parathyroid hormone secretion or action.

records.question: After H. pylori treatment, which listed noninvasive test is most suitable to document eradication?
records.explanation: A urea breath test detects persistent active H. pylori infection. Confirm eradication at least four weeks after antibiotics, with PPIs or PCABs withheld for two weeks and bismuth for four weeks. Serology can remain positive after cure and is unsuitable for this purpose.

records.question: For haemoglobin 5 g/dL and reticulocytes 9%, what is the corrected reticulocyte percentage?
records.explanation: Using the conventional normal haemoglobin of 15 g/dL, the correction is 9% multiplied by 5/15, giving 3%. This is a corrected percentage, not a reticulocyte production index; the latter also adjusts for prolonged reticulocyte maturation in severe anaemia.

records.question: Which B-cell surface molecule binds Epstein-Barr virus?
records.explanation: EBV envelope glycoprotein gp350 binds complement receptor 2, also called CD21, on B lymphocytes. Other molecules participate in fusion and entry; CD21 is the attachment receptor tested here.

records.question: A central spinal-cord cavity accompanies impaired pain and temperature sensation with preserved touch. Which diagnosis fits?
records.explanation: A syrinx can disrupt crossing spinothalamic fibres near the central canal while initially sparing dorsal-column pathways. This produces dissociated sensory loss, with pain and temperature affected more than vibration, position sense and discriminative touch.
